messages:
kevin: heads up — noticed a weird token delta in billing dashboard for a customer using streaming + tool calls. numbers don't add up to logs, looks like double-charging on retries.

maria: can you paste the example traces?

kevin: pasted below — short repro: client opens a streaming session, server sends partial tokens, triggers a tool call which returns truncated content, client reconnects and we re-run generation. logs show both attempts billed fully.

kevin: log snippet:
```
2026-03-12T15:42:01Z INFO session=start id=abc123 mode=stream
2026-03-12T15:42:02Z INFO emit_tokens count=42 attempt=1 session=abc123 route=dedicated-pool-a
2026-03-12T15:42:03Z INFO toolcall start tool=web_search parent_attempt=1
2026-03-12T15:42:03Z WARN toolcall result=truncated reason=timeout
2026-03-12T15:42:04Z INFO client reconnect attempt=2 session=abc123
2026-03-12T15:42:04Z INFO emit_tokens count=40 attempt=2 session=abc123 route=dedicated-pool-a
```

kevin: billing records show two full emits (42 + 40) but customer claims only final output should be billed; they expect prefix deduping with caching.

olga: this is the classic streaming+toolcall idempotency gap. Our current billing attributes tokens to the attempt id, and retries are independent. We never dedupe across attempts because we don't have a persistent request id that ties emitted tokens to a single logical client request.

sam: is there any existing request id? session=abc123 in logs but do we surface that to the billing pipeline?

kevin: session id is local to runtime; billing uses charge_id generated at the start of each attempt. so attempt boundary => new charge_id.

maria: two orthogonal fixes: 1) propagate session_id/consumer_request_id into billing and dedupe by (session_id, token_prefix_hash) for a short window; 2) make toolcall retries non-billable for prefix tokens if result was truncated and we resumed. both have tradeoffs.

jeff: (proposal) Add attempt.parent_session field to charge records and a best-effort prefix-kv fingerprint. Billing can then run idempotent reduce: if fingerprint seen within Xs for same session, mark as non-billable or discount. This avoids cluster-wide locking and works with eventual traces.

maria: probably need UX/console change too — show 'attempted' vs 'final' token columns and an annotation "deduped tokens" so customers understand what's happening. Must be opt-in until we validate.

olga: corner case: different routes (hosted vs dedicated) could serve different attempts; fingerprints must be canonical (sha256 of first N tokens and toolcall context). privacy: can't store raw tokens in billing DB. store only hash + length.

sam: implementation plan: runtime emits charge record with fields: consumer_request_id (session), attempt_id, route, prefix_hash, prefix_length, event_time. billing aggregator will group by consumer_request_id + prefix_hash window=90s and mark duplicates.

kevin: I'll open a RFC but wanted quick sync. can someone pick ownership for implementation spikes? olga for runtime changes, jeff for billing pipeline, maria for console UX. i'll add repro and customer trace to the RFC.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled for canary branch 'stream-dedupe' at 2026-03-18T02:30:00Z if PRs merged. :rocket:

jeff: will prototype aggregator rule this week. if we go with hashing, need to confirm collision window vs token count. prefer sha256(first 64 bytes) + prefix_len.

maria: UX note — show deduped tokens as a separate time-series in Console per-route so SREs can detect regressions. add alert if dedupe rate > 5% for a route (could indicate flappy tool calls).

kevin: sweet. thanks. filing thread in #eng-platform backlog.
